title: Aborting the interactive first-run wizard crashes the main review command instead of exiting cleanly

finding.claim: Aborting the interactive first-run wizard crashes the main review command instead of exiting cleanly
finding.evidence: On an interactive terminal with no --provider, no CODEREVIEW_PROVIDERS, and no saved config, main now unconditionally calls the setup wizard. The wizard's own docstring says EOF aborts without saving, but this call is not wrapped in any error handling, so an EOFError from input propagates out of main and terminates the process with a traceback rather than the intended setup guidance or exit code 2
finding.recommendation: Wrap the first-run '_run_setup_wizard()' call in try/except, treat abort or failure as a normal not-set-up outcome, and return 2 after printing 'userconfig.NOT_SET_UP' or a concise abort message. Also consider checking the wizard's falsey return and handling it explicitly before calling 'default_provider_specs()'.
